title: Collar Rot on Chilli - Sri Lanka

Header: Collar Rot on Chilli - Sri Lanka
Sclerotium rolfsii , Phytophthora spp., Fusarium solani , Pythium spp., Rhizoctonia spp. “Kaluthalukal” – Tamil; “Padastha kunu veema” - Sinhala

Prevention: Infected crops should be uprooted with soil and destroyed.
Deep plough and expose affected soil to bright sunlight for at least one month (in dry season).
Improve drainage (make well designed irrigation & drainage system).
Establishment of drenches; Avoid basin irrigation; Ridge and furrow method.
Plant after rainy season; Reduce plant density.
Monitoring: Regular field visits at an interval of every 3 days.
Yellowing and wilting of plants as isolated patches.
Fungal mycelium on collar region of plants & roots.
Depressed water-soaked sunken lesions in the stem.
After pulling out the affected crop, tan brown sclerotia are visible with mycelial growth (when it is caused by
Start disease management strategies at the first appearance of symptoms.
Direct Control: Remove and burn affected plants with soil.
Avoid irrigation through infected areas to do isolation of host plant.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance.
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB).
Thiophanate-methyl 70% WP; 30g/50 lit of water for 10m
Very toxic to aquatic animals; WHO class
U (Unlikely present to acute hazard in normal use)
